absent: Numeric values and bit positions of caching, present, protection and attribute flags.
Full memory layout of the attribute change descriptor and of page table entry structures.
Behavior of alias reconciliation, fault handling, large page split, static protection and permission verification helpers referenced but not routed.
Rules selecting active versus inert forms of broadcast, synchronization, installation counting and collapse accounting.
Complete cross processor flushing protocol including thresholds and single page primitives.
Definition of RAM detection, high memory bounds and physical to virtual translation beyond the single conversion shown.
Lifetime and ownership rules for page tables queued for release after collapse.

findings.text: Kernel identity map cache synchronizer that does nothing when the requested base lies beyond physical RAM or starts outside RAM, shortens the length so it ends at the top of RAM, then delegates to the virtual range attribute path to install the requested caching mode and signals invalid argument when that delegation fails.

Virtual range cache mode dispatcher that derives a page count from a byte length and chooses among uncached, combining, through and back helpers based on the requested mode, treating unrecognized modes as uncached.
Uncached request path that encodes an abstract cache mode as a protection value and passes it to a generic setter that only sets bits over a single contiguous virtual span.
Global translation cache invalidation entry that uses a hardware broadcast primitive when the processor reports support and otherwise asks every processor to run a local invalidation routine.

Attribute change lifecycle that canonicalizes the set mask and exits early when no work remains, aligns addresses down to page granularity with a warning, purges stale temporary and alias mappings, executes the protected table walk, then selects translation and cache flushing from whether anything changed and whether caching bits were touched, flushing everything on error.

Single address walker that resolves the kernel entry and diverts missing entries to a fault path, merges set and clear masks into four kilobyte entries through static and permission checks and marks translation flushing only when the entry value actually differs, and for larger entries first tries to preserve the mapping before splitting and retrying.

Batched driver that walks a requested span to completion, forces single page steps for array shaped inputs, serializes each step except for a debug allocator bypass, optionally reconciles aliases for primary changes, advances by the amount consumed, and restores the original count before returning.

Large mapping restoration flow that visits each address of array inputs or each aligned block of a contiguous span, rebuilds a mid size mapping when all small subentries agree and then attempts a larger rebuild, flushes translations once when anything changed, and finally releases retired tables while handling table accounted and non accounted pages differently.

Address resolution distinguishes page pointer arrays which yield zero for high memory and direct addresses otherwise, address arrays which index directly, and contiguous ranges which stride by page size, with an additional sign normalization on sixty four bit builds.
Cache mode decoding treats an empty cache field as the default mode and otherwise folds three scattered flag bits into a lookup index, acting as the inverse of mode to protection encoding.

Promotion requires large page processor support, suitable physical alignment, absence of a forced small page marker, and presence with identical flags and consecutive frames across every subentry, while the largest promotion additionally needs gigapage support and large immediate children.
Promotion builds a large protection value by moving the small page attribute bit to the large page position while preserving remaining bits and then marking the entry large.

Collapse accounting bumps the counter for the new level and subtracts the fanout from the lower level when enabled, emits collapse events only after the system is fully running, and applies only when the virtual address is valid and its frame sits inside a recorded mapped interval.

Attribute walks serialize each step with a dedicated attribute lock and hold the initial address space under read protection during the walk, collapse holds that space under write protection and reuses the attribute lock and the top level table lock while scanning, and broadcast invalidation holds preemption disabled across broadcast and synchronization.

Flush paths require interrupts enabled except during early boot, skip cache work when no caching attribute changed, fall back to a full flush when line flush support is absent or when forced by size or error, and order the per page line flush loop over present entries with barriers.

Callers must provide page aligned addresses while unaligned inputs are truncated with a one time warning, stale mappings are purged before walking to prevent aliasing, and uncached requests use a weaker minus variant because the helpers cannot override true device memory.
Cache mode table index is a three bit value assembled from three distinct flag bit positions.
Small to large protection conversion clears both attribute bit positions and then relocates the small page attribute bit to the large page attribute position.

An entry counts as present when either its present bit or its protection none bit is set, counts as empty only when all bits outside an erratum mask are clear, and flag extraction reads the native value masked to flag bits.

Table helpers read native entry values to obtain flags, frame numbers and protections, rebuild entries from frame plus protection pairs, translate table entries to backing pages, and update upper level entries through either a paravirtualized or a native store as selected by configuration.

Broadcast and synchronization helpers have active and inert forms chosen by configuration, where the active broadcast checks alignment and issues a broadcast primitive and the active synchronization forbids migration, issues a sync primitive, and repeats it when a processor erratum is present.
Small page installation counting and collapse level accounting each have an enabled form that updates counters and a disabled form that does nothing, selected by configuration.

Range cache flushing aligns the start down to the processor line size and steps line by line with a runtime patched flush instruction, and ordering barriers are likewise runtime patched between a locked update and a fence based on processor capability.
